q-50331.name: Question 1
q-50331.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/d930c097ed0ddfa454d7f443112c2d9e233e29521e8950fcc4738e742dd3d8dc.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x=\frac{6}{y}$ and $x=7-y$ for $y\in [1,6]$ is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the line $x=-3.$  Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
q-50331.worked_solution:
Let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/edea788893771f13f3afc7d9f49e8f1dead4e9b589ca78ef160b9bddccf867c5.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=\frac{6}{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=7-y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=7-y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/48df22796616a48f9e9ed56474ced12392905e976fdec064b401894f30cbf49b.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}[\,(7-y)-(-3)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}{[10-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=\frac{6}{y}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/f3240bb3d94231ae5b786b01b2fe11f9e0ea7971978e54f26a4e36b84af71a28.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}{[\,(\frac{6}{y})-(-3)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}{[\frac{6}{y}+3]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}{[10-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}{[\frac{6}{y}+3]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{6}({[10-y]}^{2}-{[\frac{6}{y}+3]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

The region enclosed by the curves x=6y and x=7−y for y∈[1,6] is rotated 360∘ about the line x=−3. Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?

a
π∫06([10−y]2−[6y+3]2)dy
b
π∫16([7−y]2−[6y]2)dy
c
π∫16([6y+3]2)dy
d
π∫−6−1([10−y]2−[6y+3]2)dy
e
π∫16([10−y]2−[6y+3]2)dy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve x=6y, and

  • leaves through the outer curve x=7−y.

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve x=7−y.

The corresponding volume is given by Vouter=π∫16[(right)−(left)]2dy=π∫16[(7−y)−(−3)]2dy=π∫16[10−y]2dy.

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve x=6y.

The corresponding volume is given by Vinner=π∫16[(right)−(left)]2dy=π∫16[(6y)−(−3)]2dy=π∫16[6y+3]2dy.

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as V=Vouter−Vinner=π∫16[10−y]2dy−π∫16[6y+3]2dy=π∫16([10−y]2−[6y+3]2)dy.

The region enclosed by the curves $x=-\frac{10}{y}$ and $x=y-7$ for $y\in [2,5]$ is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the line $x=-1.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
q-50428.worked_solution:
Let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/987999e84c2b22c8b90ecb0381518e7504d0b792ecebb067a7221653422b3e89.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=-\frac{10}{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=y-7.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y-7.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/f8c250c5fbf20980050a1e86f4ac5c91bff7b24bfc7ce5394f33c87703139026.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}[\,(-1)-(y-7)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[6-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=-\frac{10}{y}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/64b440be918c616eb07f05f7f09cb8e14ed649f677afc5f40f66f47ec34ed87e.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[\,(-1)-(-\frac{10}{y})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[\frac{10}{y}-1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[6-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[\frac{10}{y}-1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}({[6-y]}^{2}-{[\frac{10}{y}-1]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

b

π∫16([6−y]2−[10y−1]2)dy

π∫−25([6−y]2−[10y−1]2)dy

Let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve x=−10y, and

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve x=y−7.

The corresponding volume is given by Vouter=π∫25[(right)−(left)]2dy=π∫25[(−1)−(y−7)]2dy=π∫25[6−y]2dy.

The region above enclosed by the curves $y=\sqrt{x}$ and $y={x}^{2}$ for $x\in [0,1]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=-1.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
q-350910.worked_solution:
First, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/bd558d08aa48a17d04b9c3929a5b49a21e5fd7bde8ebfe4a07f8cabfd824b981.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y={x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y=\sqrt{x}.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=\sqrt{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/b8c8e0216a8ee045a9d7a570bc26d1765fc54e2110b1c1d2fbbc8f59d1ec22ef.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\sqrt{x})-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[\sqrt{x}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y={x}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/4cd4e1fb0ad340da9a2e146fa261c6a50e4578f1b77564c8d6a5c6a2f27c81f9.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,({x}^{2})-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{2}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[\sqrt{x}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{2}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({(\sqrt{x}+1)}^{2}-{({x}^{2}+1)}^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(2\sqrt{x}-{x}^{4}-2{x}^{2}+x)\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3/2}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}-\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{4}{3}(1)^{3/2}-\frac{1}{5}(1)^{5}-\frac{2}{3}(1)^{3}+\frac{1}{2}(1)^{2})-0] \\  & =\frac{29\pi }{30}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, since we are rotating about a vertical axis, we need to solve the equation of our second curve for $x:$

$$

$$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x={y}^{2}+2,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=y+4.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/262546bf3f1d1c9025d23b9fb134c9de7b5299c7b6383563531dffa62244163d.png)

$$

$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x={y}^{2}+2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/cefab13ca3d09fcf596e7906384c2efd1718c289783792f1b0ff950632c823ad.png)

$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of our solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{2}({[y+6]}^{2}-{[{y}^{2}+4]}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{2}({y}^{2}+12y+36-({y}^{4}+8{y}^{2}+16))\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{2}(12y+20-{y}^{4}-7{y}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(6{y}^{2}+20y-\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}-\frac{7{y}^{3}}{3})|}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\pi [\,(6\cdot {2}^{2}+20\cdot 2-\frac{{2}^{5}}{5}-\frac{7\cdot {2}^{3}}{3})\,-\,(6-20+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{7}{3})\,] \\  & =\pi (\frac{584}{15}-(-\frac{172}{15})) \\  & =\frac{252\pi }{5}.\end{aligned}
